world.title: Harardhere Authorities and SNA Deliver Emergency Relief to Flood
world.description: MOGADISHU — The administration of Xarardheere district, led by District Commissioner Aseyr Ibrahim Matan, alongside the Somali National Army (SNA), delivered emergency assistance to communities affected by heavy rains that have battered the district in recent days. The rains caused significant impact on the local population, particularly in neighborhoods including Howlwadaag and Tuulo Cali Dagaay, where residents were left facing urgent needs requiring relief and support. The district administration and SNA forces carried out the relief efforts to assist affected communities, emphasizing the importance of cooperation and reaching out to people facing hardship. A Local Response Within a National Crisis The flooding in Xarardheere is part of a wider pattern of extreme weather affecting Somalia as the Deyr rainy season begins under Super El Niño conditions. As reported in FTL Somalia’s coverage of the SoDMA warnings, the Somali Disaster Management Agency had placed Xarardheere and 28 other districts across 14 regions on high alert for riverine and flash flooding. The flood risk in Xarardheere was specifically highlighted in the latest FAO-SWALIM forecast. As detailed in FTL Somalia’s coverage of the weekly forecast, heavy cumulative rainfall of 100-150 millimetres was expected over a localized area near the coast in Xarardheere district, with moderate rainfall of 50-100 millimetres forecast over most of the district. The regional impact has been severe. As reported in FTL Somalia’s coverage of the Hudur floods, flash floods in the South West State displaced 37 households. In Mogadishu, heavy rains submerged roads, disrupting schools, businesses and transportation, as detailed in FTL Somalia’s coverage of the Mogadishu floods. The Need for Preparedness and Coordination The response by local authorities and the military reflects the multi-layered nature of disaster response in Somalia, where federal, regional, and local actors, alongside humanitarian partners, must coordinate to reach affected populations. science.title: Long non-coding RNA NEAT1 drives nuclear condensates regulating gene expression and ferroptosis vulnerability in pancreatic cancer cells
science.description: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is an aggressive malignancy with poor patient outcomes due to development of tumor cell drug resistance impacting treatment efficacy. Shifts in tumor cell transcriptional subtypes from well-differentiated classical to poorly differentiated basal-like cells can drive PDAC chemotherapeutic resistance. Such transcriptomic changes have been linked to cellular metabolic states, but how coordination of transcriptional and metabolic programs is mediated at the molecular level remains unclear. The stress-responsive long noncoding RNA NEAT1, an essential constituent of nuclear condensates called paraspeckles, has been associated with classical PDAC and was previously linked to regulation of cellular metabolism. In this study, we utilized a high-throughput drug screening approach in NEAT1-deficient cancer cells to uncover functional metabolic targets in these cells, identifying ferroptosis via GPX4 inhibition as a major vulnerability of cells lacking paraspeckles. We find that the paraspeckle-forming isoform of NEAT1 is central to ferroptosis suppression, and we extend these results into PDAC cell line models with genetic suppression or activation of NEAT1. We find that NEAT1-nucleated paraspeckles underlie the expression program tied to the classical PDAC subtype and promote ferroptosis resistance. We pinpoint the paraspeckle-suppressive RNA-binding protein QKI, associated with basal-like PDAC, as a positive regulator of ferroptosis susceptibility, possibly through its suppression of paraspeckles. These results link NEAT1 and regulation of paraspeckle condensates to subtype-specific ferroptosis susceptibility in PDAC and offer novel avenues for targeting metabolic vulnerabilities of pancreatic cancer cells on the basis of transcriptional subtype.

science.title: Coupled analytical and finite element investigation of dynamic and cyclic response in cracked functionally graded beams
science.description: Offshore and marine structures increasingly utilise Functionally Graded Materials (FGMs) because of their superior stiffness and enhanced resistance to damage under combined vibration and cyclic loading induced by waves, wind and operational conditions. This study presents a combined analytical and finite element investigation into the dynamic behaviour of a cracked FGM cantilever beam compared with eight conventional offshore structural steels. A fracture-mechanics-based analytical model, incorporating crack-induced flexibility and stiffness degradation under cyclic loading within a continuum damage mechanics framework, was developed to predict the beam’s natural frequencies and validated against finite element results, with deviations below 2%. The postulated cracks were represented by predefined notches to simulate pre-existing structural damage or defects, with crack depth ratios of a/h = 0.233, 0.333, 0.4, & 0.5 introduced at different locations along the beam length. A nonlinear finite element model developed in ABAQUS was subsequently used to evaluate stress evolution, strain accumulation, and hysteretic force-displacement response under displacement-controlled cyclic loading. As the crack depth ratio increased, both the natural frequency and stiffness decreased, whereas stress concentration, strain accumulation, and hysteresis loop width increased, indicating greater energy dissipation and progressive stiffness degradation. Compared with conventional offshore steels, the FGM beam consistently exhibited higher natural frequencies, lower displacement amplitudes, and stable cyclic behaviour without significant strength degradation. The proposed analytical-numerical framework was further validated against published experimental results, confirming its reliability for assessing the coupled vibration and cyclic behaviour of cracked FGM beams for offshore structural applications.
